items.name: animated-number
items.title: Animated number
items.description: Smooth interruptible number transitions with locale formatting and a stable accessible value.
items.docs: Data in, callbacks out. Locale defaults to en-US; pass your application locale explicitly. Reduced motion shows the final state immediately.

items.description: An interactive example with real state changes and accessible controls.

items.title: Copy Field
items.description: A selectable code field with clipboard feedback and an error fallback.

items.name: copy-field-demo
items.title: Copy Field demo

items.name: email-addresses-section
items.title: Email addresses section
items.description: The email addresses on an account: which one is primary, which are verified, add another, make one primary or remove it, each step explained in the row.
items.docs: Controlled: keep emails in state and update it in each callback. Every callback may return a promise; the row shows a busy state and a rejection is shown in words. Throw an Error with a message from onAdd to explain why an address was refused; the other callbacks show a general message. The primary address cannot be removed and the row says why; removing any other address asks inside the row.

items.name: email-addresses-section-demo
items.title: Email addresses section demo
items.description: A working preview of Email addresses section.

items.name: public-profile-section
items.title: Public profile section
items.description: Edit how others see you: picture, display name, @username with a live availability hint, bio with a counter, links, and a preview that updates as you type.
items.docs: profile is the saved profile; the draft lives inside until Save, and a new profile passed back replaces it. onSave receives the cleaned-up draft and, when a new picture was chosen, the File to upload as the second argument (profile.avatar of a new picture is only a temporary preview address: store the real URL you get back). onCheckUsername(username) resolves true when the name is free and is only asked for names that follow the rules and differ from the saved one.

items.name: public-profile-section-demo
items.title: Public profile section demo
items.description: A working preview of Public profile section.

items.name: appearance-settings
items.title: Appearance settings
items.description: Choose how the interface looks: three theme preview cards, a density choice with a live sample list, and an optional font choice, all applied at once.
items.docs: Controlled: keep value in state, update it in onChange and apply theme, density and font yourself. The theme previews paint their own palette, so each one is true on any page theme. Leave systemTheme out and System reads the browser; pass fonts={[]} to hide the font choice.

items.name: appearance-settings-demo
items.title: Appearance settings demo
items.description: A working preview of Appearance settings.

items.name: accessibility-preferences
items.title: Accessibility preferences
items.description: The settings people reach for first: text size with a live sample, motion, contrast, underlined links and keyboard hints, each applied at once.
items.docs: textSize is an index into TEXT_SIZE_STEPS (from steps.ts): apply its scale to your root font size. motion and contrast are plain values for a data attribute or a CSS variable; applying them is yours. Leave systemMotion out and Follow system reads prefers-reduced-motion from the browser.

items.name: accessibility-preferences-demo
items.title: Accessibility preferences demo
items.description: A working preview of Accessibility preferences.

items.name: language-region-section
items.title: Language and region section
items.description: Language, country, time zone and formats in one card, with a live sample line showing the date, time and number exactly as they will read.
items.docs: value is the saved setting; the draft lives inside until Save, and a new value passed back replaces it. The preview is formatted with Intl from the draft, always with a time zone, at a fixed moment (sampleDate, a date or an ISO string) so server and browser render the same text. languages are written in their own names; timeZones are IANA ids, grouped by their offset at that moment; locale is the language the country names are shown in.

items.name: language-region-section-demo
items.title: Language and region section demo
items.description: A working preview of Language and region section.

items.name: privacy-settings-section
items.title: Privacy settings section
items.description: Who can see your profile and what you share: visibility as choice cards, then switches for activity, search and analytics, each saying what it changes for others.
items.docs: Controlled: keep value in state and set it in onChange. Changes apply at once; return a promise from onChange and the status line shows Saving, then the confirmation or an error. Applying the settings (who may read the profile, robots tags, analytics) is yours.

items.name: privacy-settings-section-demo
items.title: Privacy settings section demo
items.description: A working preview of Privacy settings section.

items.name: connected-accounts
items.title: Connected accounts
items.description: The sign-in providers linked to an account: who is connected, as whom and since when, with connect and disconnect per row and a guard on the last way in.
items.docs: An account counts as connected once it has an identity or a connection date. Without canDisconnect, the only connected provider is protected; pass your own rule when a password or passkey also counts as a way in. protectedHint says how to add another way in: a tooltip on the protected provider, and plain text under the row on touch screens and in narrow rows where a tooltip cannot open. Dates are shown in the timeZone you pass (default UTC) so server and browser agree.

items.name: connected-accounts-demo
items.title: Connected accounts demo
items.description: A working preview of Connected accounts.

items.name: data-export-section
items.title: Data export section
items.description: The right of access without a support ticket: pick what to include and a format, request the export, and follow earlier ones by status and expiry.
items.docs: Data in, callbacks out: pass the groups, the earlier exports and onRequest. While an export is preparing (or onRequest is pending) the button rests and the card says it will email the person; add the new export to `exports` with status "preparing" and flip it to "ready" with a size, expiresAt and href when it is done. Dates use the locale and timeZone props (UTC by default); pass `now` to pin the relative "Expires in 5 days". title, description and headingLevel (2 or 3) rename the heading and set its level.

items.name: data-export-section-demo
items.title: Data export section demo
items.description: A working preview of Data export section.

items.name: billing-details-section
items.title: Billing details section
items.description: What appears on invoices: company, address, a tax number checked for format and live, billing emails as chips and a reference, saved as one block.
items.docs: onSave may return a message (shown by the Save button), an object of messages keyed by field (shown against the fields), or nothing. onValidateTaxId resolves true or false for the live "Valid" or "Could not verify"; it runs once the number has the right shape. taxIdLabels adds or changes a country's label, example and pattern over the built-in table in tax-ids.ts. title, description and headingLevel (2 or 3) rename the heading and set its level.

items.name: billing-details-section-demo
items.title: Billing details section demo
items.description: A working preview of Billing details section.

items.name: email-preference-center
items.title: Email preference center
items.description: The page behind 'manage your emails': a frequency per list, a pause for 30 days, and unsubscribe from everything behind one inline confirmation.
items.docs: Works without a signed-in session: pass the address (it is shown partly masked) and save each change from onChange, which may return a promise. A list's frequencies default to Off, Weekly and Monthly. Up to four steps sit side by side (on a phone, long labels become a menu) and more than four are always a menu. The value "off" is what Unsubscribe from everything sets. Leave out onPause, onResume or onUnsubscribeAll to drop that part of the page. Controlled with value, or uncontrolled with defaultValue. title, description and headingLevel (2 or 3) rename the heading and set its level.

items.name: email-preference-center-demo
items.title: Email preference center demo
items.description: A working preview of Email preference center.

items.name: workspace-profile-section
items.title: Workspace profile section
items.description: A workspace's name, URL, default time zone and language, with a live preview of the address, a warning before links change and a save that lights up.
items.docs: The slug is limited to lowercase letters, numbers and hyphens as you type. onCheckSlug resolves true when an address is free; it is asked after a pause in typing and only for an address that differs from the saved one. Changing the slug shows a warning in words before saving. timeZones takes IANA names, listed in the order you pass them, and languages takes { value, label } pairs; both lists are searchable (a language is also found by its name in `locale`, so "German" finds Deutsch) and have sensible defaults in defaults.ts. While Save runs the fields are locked. Pass the saved workspace back as `workspace` after onSave and the form follows. title, description and headingLevel (2 or 3) rename the heading and set its level.

items.name: workspace-profile-section-demo
items.title: Workspace profile section demo
items.description: A working preview of Workspace profile section.

items.name: branding-settings
items.title: Branding settings
items.description: How a workspace looks to its customers: logos for light and dark, an icon and a brand colour with a contrast check, and live page and email previews.
items.docs: Images are URLs: onUpload receives the chosen file (only SVG and PNG get that far) and resolves to the address it can be shown from, and Save hands back the same four values. An address that turns out not to draw is taken back with a message, so a broken image is never saved. The colour is checked against white and black text (minContrast 4.5 is WCAG AA, 7 is AAA) and against a white page; one that fails is not applied and the reason is shown. colors sets the swatches. The previews are drawn on literal white, because they show the customer's page, not your product. title, description and headingLevel (2 or 3) rename the heading and set its level.

items.name: branding-settings-demo
items.title: Branding settings demo
items.description: A working preview of Branding settings.

items.name: authenticator-setup
items.title: Authenticator setup
items.description: Two-step sign-in setup in one card: scan the QR code or type the key, then confirm with the first six-digit code. It works without a camera.
items.docs: The block draws no QR code: pass your own SVG or image in qr (draw it from the otpauth address with a QR library). It is wrapped with alt text that carries the key, so setup works without a camera, and it sits on a white tile, so keep it dark on light. onVerify resolves true or false; a wrong code is announced and cleared. After success the card shows what you pass as next, usually a button to the recovery codes, and the focus moves to that confirmation so the button is one Tab away. title, description and headingLevel (2 or 3) rename the heading and set its level.

items.name: authenticator-setup-demo
items.title: Authenticator setup demo
items.description: A working preview of Authenticator setup.

items.name: recovery-codes-section
items.title: Recovery codes section
items.description: Recovery codes shown once with copy, download and print, and a checkbox people must tick to confirm they saved them before they can continue.
items.docs: Codes of any length work: they sit two to a row while the longest fits and one to a row when it does not. Pass plain strings for fresh codes, or { code, used } to show which were spent (they are struck through and read Used). With onContinue the block asks for "I have saved these codes" and keeps Continue locked until it is ticked; with onRegenerate a new set is offered behind an inline confirmation, and the new codes come back through `codes`. Print hides everything on the page except a plain sheet of the unused codes. Without onDownload the block saves recovery-codes.txt itself. title, description and headingLevel (2 or 3) rename the heading and set its level.

items.name: recovery-codes-section-demo
items.title: Recovery codes section demo
items.description: A working preview of Recovery codes section.

items.name: transfer-ownership-card
items.title: Transfer ownership card
items.description: Hand a workspace to another member: pick the new owner, read what changes, and confirm by typing the workspace name in a dialog that names what you are giving away.
items.docs: members are the people you would allow as the new owner; a member with disabledReason is listed but cannot be chosen. onTransfer(memberId) may be async: resolve to nothing when it worked, or resolve to (or throw) a message when it failed, and the card keeps the choice and shows it. Leave consequences out for a default list that names the new owner, and confirmDescription out for the default dialog text; say what is true for your product in both. onCancel adds a Cancel button for flows the person can leave.

items.name: transfer-ownership-card-demo
items.title: Transfer ownership card demo
items.description: A working preview of Transfer ownership card.

items.name: early-access-features
items.title: Early access features
items.description: Let people opt into previews: each feature with an Alpha or Beta badge, a switch, what changes and how to undo it, and links to give feedback.
items.docs: Controlled: keep features in state and update enabled in onToggle. Return a promise from onToggle and the switch moves at once and stays busy until it settles; if it rejects, the switch goes back and the row says so. effect and undo are the words shown after a switch is turned on. A feature with disabledReason is locked and says why in text.

items.name: early-access-features-demo
items.title: Early access features demo
items.description: A working preview of Early access features.

items.name: bulk-select-menu
items.title: Bulk select menu
items.description: The header checkbox with a menu for choosing what to select: all, none, unread, starred, with the mixed state and the count in words.
items.docs: Controlled: derive state (none, some or all) from your own selection and keep the selection in your callbacks. The checkbox runs onSelectAll when nothing is selected and onSelectNone otherwise. Each criterion shows the number it would select and is disabled at 0. After every choice a polite message says what was selected.

items.name: bulk-select-menu-demo
items.title: Bulk select menu demo
items.description: A working preview of Bulk select menu.

items.name: copy-as-menu
items.title: Copy as menu
items.description: Copy the same thing in the format the next tool wants: a split button whose menu offers Markdown, JSON, cURL or plain text and remembers the last choice.
items.docs: Each format's serialize() runs only when someone copies in that format, and may return a promise. Pass format and onFormatChange to keep the last choice yourself (in local storage, say), or defaultFormat to leave it to the button. Picking a format in the menu copies in it at once. Set as on a format when it reads badly after Copy as: "plain text" for Plain text. Formats carry functions, so build them in a client component.

items.name: copy-as-menu-demo
items.title: Copy as menu demo
items.description: A working preview of Copy as menu.

items.name: add-to-calendar-button
items.title: Add to calendar button
items.description: Adds an event to the calendar people use, Google, Outlook, Apple or an .ics file, built from one event object with the time zone handled.
items.docs: A start without an offset (2026-11-12T19:00) is read in the event's timeZone; a Date or a string ending in Z or +01:00 is an exact moment. Give end or durationMinutes (default 60). All-day events take a date, and end is the last day. buildIcs, buildGoogleUrl and buildOutlookUrl are pure functions in calendar.ts that return null for an event that cannot be read. Pass uid so an edited event updates the first one in the calendar.

items.name: add-to-calendar-button-demo
items.title: Add to calendar button demo
items.description: A working preview of Add to calendar button.

items.name: directions-button
items.title: Directions button
items.description: Get directions in the maps app people use: Apple Maps on iPhone, Google Maps elsewhere, Waze if they prefer, and the address to copy as a fallback.
items.docs: Give the destination an address (with its name, so the pin is labelled) or latitude and longitude; a name alone is not enough and disables the button with the reason. Without apps, Apple Maps comes first on iPhone and iPad and Google Maps elsewhere, decided after mount. Waze only drives. The link builders in directions.ts are pure and return null for a place that cannot be used.

items.name: directions-button-demo
items.title: Directions button demo
items.description: A working preview of Directions button.

items.name: save-contact-button
items.title: Save contact button
items.description: Save a person or business to the address book: it builds a vCard in the browser from one contact object and downloads it, with no server involved.
items.docs: The file is a vCard 3.0 with escaped text, lines folded at 75 octets and labelled phone, email and address types. On an iPhone it opens the Add Contact sheet. The accessible name adds who it is for, and a contact without a name disables the button with the reason. buildVCard in vcard.ts is pure and returns null without a name, so the same text can become a QR code.

items.name: save-contact-button-demo
items.title: Save contact button demo
items.description: A working preview of Save contact button.

items.name: follow-button
items.title: Follow button
items.description: Follow, Following and Requested in one button: optimistic, with a follower count, a clear way to unfollow and a rollback message when the request fails.
items.docs: Controlled: keep status and count in state and update both in onFollow and onUnfollow before they resolve. The button answers at once and rolls back with a message if the promise rejects; presses are ignored while a request is pending. Resolve onFollow with "requested" when the account needs approval, or pass isPrivate to ask for it up front; unfollowing a private account asks once. defaultStatus leaves the status to the button, and the count then stays as given for that starting status and moves with the button. The error line is wider than the button and widens the control with it, so where you right-align the button pass className="items-end" (or sm:items-end) and it keeps its right edge when a request fails. The accessible name stays "Follow <name>" and aria-pressed carries the state, while the visible word changes to Following or Requested.

items.name: follow-button-demo
items.title: Follow button demo
items.description: A working preview of Follow button.

items.name: like-button
items.title: Like button
items.description: A like button where the count is the point: it answers at once, rolls the number, plays one quiet ring and tells screen readers the exact count.
items.docs: Controlled: keep liked and count in state and update both in onToggle once the request has succeeded; the button already shows the new state while it waits, and rolls back with a message if onToggle rejects. defaultLiked leaves the state to the button, and count then stays as written for that starting state and moves with the button. Counts above 999 abbreviate by locale (1.2K, 1,2 Mio.) while the accessible name and the tooltip keep the exact number. Pass names to make the tooltip read "Liked by ...", and any @rhs-ui/icons glyph as icon: it is drawn filled once liked.

items.name: like-button-demo
items.title: Like button demo
items.description: A working preview of Like button.

items.name: vote-buttons
items.title: Vote buttons
items.description: Up and down arrows around a score for questions, answers and feature requests: one vote each, changeable, with the score announced.
items.docs: Controlled: keep value and score in state and update both in onVote once the request has succeeded. onVote receives "up", "down" or "none" (pressing the chosen arrow again clears the vote). The control moves the score by the right amount while the request is on its way, including two for a switch from down to up, and puts both back with a message in a bubble beside the control (to the right of a vertical one, to the left of a row, whichever side has room) if onVote rejects. score is written for the vote the control starts in. Set subject to name what is voted on, and allowDownvote={false} for a single arrow with a count.

items.name: vote-buttons-demo
items.title: Vote buttons demo
items.description: A working preview of Vote buttons.

items.name: watch-button
items.title: Watch button
items.description: A watch button with levels: all activity, mentions only or nothing, as a split button whose words and bell always say what you will be told.
items.docs: Controlled: keep level and count in state and update both in onLevelChange once the request has succeeded. The main button switches between the last level that was on and "ignore"; the chevron opens a radio menu. Pass levels to change the words (id must stay all, mentions or ignore) and subject for the accessible name ("Watching this issue, all activity"). The count moves by one when watching starts or stops. A rejected onLevelChange rolls everything back with a message.

items.name: watch-button-demo
items.title: Watch button demo
items.description: A working preview of Watch button.

items.name: approval-buttons
items.title: Approval buttons
items.description: Approve and Reject as one decision: a reason when rejecting, who decided and when, and a short window to change your mind.
items.docs: Uncontrolled it runs by itself: Approve and Reject call onApprove and onReject (each may return a promise and shows its own busy and error state), then the status line takes over with Change decision for undoWindow seconds. Controlled, pass status, decidedBy, decidedAt and reason, and set status back to pending in onChangeDecision. Reject always asks for a reason first (requireReason makes it required). Pass locale and timeZone so the time reads the same on the server and in the browser. A decision made here shows just the time on the day it was made and adds the date on any other day; a time you pass in decidedAt always carries its date, so a page rendered on the server reads the same once it has loaded. In a narrow space Change decision drops under the sentence. The control holds no form of its own, so it can sit inside yours, and Ctrl or Cmd with Enter confirms a rejection.

items.name: approval-buttons-demo
items.title: Approval buttons demo
items.description: A working preview of Approval buttons.

items.name: social-sign-in-buttons
items.title: Social sign-in buttons
items.description: Continue-with buttons for sign-in providers: monogram marks instead of brand logos, a last-used tag first in the list, and one busy state.
items.docs: Pass providers (id, label and an optional mark) and onSelect(id). While onSelect runs, that provider's button shows a spinner and the others disable; a rejection puts a message under the list. For a redirect flow pass busy yourself. lastUsed moves a provider first and tags it. The default marks are neutral monogram tiles built from the name (GH for GitHub, G for Google, one letter more when two would match), so no trademarked logo ships; bring your own with mark. In a narrow row the name moves up against its mark so it still fits. layout is stacked, grid or icons (square buttons with a tooltip); the list is labelled for screen readers.

items.name: social-sign-in-buttons-demo
items.title: Social sign-in buttons demo
items.description: A working preview of Social sign-in buttons.

items.name: translate-toggle
items.title: Translate toggle
items.description: Translate a review or comment and back to the original with one quiet control that shows loading, translated-from and failed states.
items.docs: Nothing is translated unless you pass onTranslate(text), which returns the translated string and runs only when the control is pressed; the result is kept, so going back and forth asks once. Uncontrolled it manages its own state. To control it, pass state with onStateChange, and translation once the state is translated. sourceLocale and locale are the language codes that mark each version with lang, so screen readers switch voice. labels changes the words of the control for a site that is not in English.

items.name: translate-toggle-demo
items.title: Translate toggle demo
items.description: A working preview of Translate toggle.

items.name: use-location-button
items.title: Use location button
items.description: A Use my location button that handles every outcome in words: finding you, found with its accuracy, blocked, unavailable and timed out.
items.docs: navigator.geolocation is called only when the button is pressed, never on load. onLocate receives latitude, longitude and accuracy in metres and nothing is sent anywhere; onError receives denied, unavailable or timeout. Where the Permissions API exists, a site that is already blocked says so before the first press. The button renders nothing where there is no geolocation. Pass geolocation to supply your own source (a native shell, or a stub to try every outcome), and labels to change the words.

items.name: use-location-button-demo
items.title: Use location button demo
items.description: A working preview of Use location button.

items.name: keep-awake-toggle
items.title: Keep awake toggle
items.description: A switch that keeps the screen on for recipes, scripts and slides with the Wake Lock API, taking it again after a tab switch.
items.docs: The lock is requested when the switch is turned on, requested again when the tab becomes visible (browsers let go of it while a tab is hidden) and released when it is turned off or the page goes. Nothing is requested on load: a switch that starts on (defaultOn or on) asks for the lock at the first touch or key press. If the browser refuses, the switch returns to off, onChange(false) is called and one line says why. Where the Wake Lock API does not exist the component renders nothing. Pass wakeLock to supply your own source.

items.name: keep-awake-toggle-demo
items.title: Keep awake toggle demo
items.description: A working preview of Keep awake toggle.

items.name: listen-button
items.title: Listen button
items.description: Listen to this article with the browser's own speech: play, pause and stop, a choice of speed, and the sentence being read highlighted.
items.docs: Pass text, or targetRef for an element whose text is read sentence by sentence (the sentence being read is highlighted with the CSS Custom Highlight API, without touching your markup; mark anything that should not be read with data-listen-skip). lang picks the voice and how sentences are cut. The button reads in sentences, which also avoids Chrome stopping long utterances, and stops when the page is hidden or unmounts. Progress is shown as sentences, not time. A page has one voice: pressing a second button stops the first, and if anything else cuts the speech off the button goes back to rest. Where the browser has no speech synthesis it renders nothing; pass engine to supply your own.

items.name: listen-button-demo
items.title: Listen button demo
items.description: A working preview of Listen button.
